speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Introduced Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2014 to 2015, seeking just over $8.4 billion from the Consolidated Revenue Fund, including about $3.2 billion for the Department of Communications to continue the National Broadband Network rollout and just under $2.5 billion in capital funding for the Department of Defence.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Moved to suspend standing orders so debate on the Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2014-2015 would proceed as a cognate debate with other appropriation bills, with combined questions on their second reading, detail and third reading stages unless varied by a minister's motion.

speeches.speaker: Catherine King
speeches.brief: Argued the budget launches a fundamental attack on Medicare, citing a $50 billion cut from public hospitals starting in 35 days, disputed the Treasurer's claim that Australians visit the doctor 11 times a year on average when the true figure is fewer than seven, and reported an Aboriginal medical service would need an extra $350,000 a year to keep employing doctors under the new GP tax.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: Tallied 126 government programs cut in the appropriation bills, including $100 million from the More Support for Students with Disabilities program without a Gonski replacement, $43.5 million from the ABC and SBS plus abolition of the $196.8 million Australia Network, and $7.6 billion cut from overseas development aid over the forward estimates.

speeches.speaker: Philip Ruddock
speeches.brief: Declared that the appropriation bills for the 2014 to 2015 and 2013 to 2014 financial years stood referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration from 1.30 pm that day.

speeches.speaker: Kate Ellis
speeches.brief: Argued that the budget delivers the biggest cut to schools in the nation's history, citing $30 billion ripped from Australian schools after years five and six of Gonski funding were dumped, leaving schools $6½ billion worse off in federal funding.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Defended Labor's $14.7 billion Gonski investment benefiting the roughly 21,000 students across 45 schools in his Moreton electorate, cited reports of degree costs rising by as much as 33 per cent, and said Australia's net debt peaks at just one-seventh the level of comparable advanced economies while retaining a AAA credit rating shared by only eight countries.

speeches.speaker: Warren Entsch
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the budget, highlighting $6.7 billion committed to the Bruce Highway, $210 million for Cape York infrastructure, and $1.4 million to help establish the Mossman Botanical Gardens, contrasting these funded commitments with what he called hollow Labor promises.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the budget, noting Labor's debt interest bill of $1 billion a month could otherwise fund more than 10 new base hospitals a year, said overall health spending would rise from $64.5 billion to $74.8 billion by 2017-18, and highlighted around 80,000 more students gaining access to higher education by 2018.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: Argued the budget offers a credible, honest path to surplus in contrast to the former Treasurer's record, recalling his March 2008 promise of a $21.7 billion surplus that became a $27.1 billion deficit, and said the budget would cut projected 2023-24 gross debt from $667 billion to $389 billion while this year's interest bill alone is $14.4 billion.

speeches.speaker: Chris Hayes
speeches.brief: Argued the budget hits his low-income electorate hardest, estimating the new GP and medicine co-payments will cost Western Sydney families over $100 million a year, and said switching pension indexation to CPI would have left pensioners $1,670 worse off over the past five years, saving the government $400 million.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Hogan
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the budget's fiscal sustainability, saying Labor's $12 billion a year interest bill could otherwise build schools and hospitals, highlighted more than $5 billion in federal funding to maintain the Pacific Highway duplication at an 80 per cent share, and noted a new 50-50 bridge renewal program for ageing timber bridges that can cost up to $1 million each to repair.

speeches.speaker: Melissa Price
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the budget's regional health measures for her Durack electorate, noting 23 per cent of the population is predicted to be 65 or over by 2050, welcomed $56 million in new funding for renal dialysis services across regional Western Australia, and reported $13 million over four years for an additional 3,000 places in the Clontarf Foundation's Indigenous sports academy program.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Byrne
speeches.brief: Argued the budget's reinstated fuel excise indexation, currently 38.143c a litre, would have reached 55c a litre had it continued since 2001, disproportionately hitting outer-suburban families, and said the Monash Health hospital network in his electorate stands to lose $122,536,072 in funding between 2014 and 2018.

speeches.speaker: Clare O'Neil
speeches.brief: Told the story of Hotham constituent Danny, a kidney transplant recipient and forklift driver who pays $139.70 a month for medication and will face an extra $25 for drugs plus $7 for pathology and doctor visits, and contrasted the Treasurer's roughly $7,000 weekly income with the electorate's median of about $518 a week.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Contended the budget repairs a 'fiscal train wreck' left by Labor, reducing the tax burden by $5.7 billion while warning that LNG project approvals now take two years longer than in 2007, adding $30 million to $40 million a month to project costs, and said 512,000 small business jobs were lost over Labor's six years due to reduced access to finance.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Quoted a Bendigo primary school student's letter accusing the Prime Minister of unfairness, cited $25 million to be cut from Bendigo Health over five years, and warned that a Bendigo medical student would have faced a $200,000 degree cost and could not have afforded to study under the government's higher education changes.

speeches.speaker: Alannah MacTiernan
speeches.brief: Criticised the government's narrow view of its economic role, and said she would focus on cuts to science and research agencies contained in the appropriation bills.

speeches.speaker: Mark Butler
speeches.brief: Argued the government manufactured a budget crisis, citing the Treasurer's MYEFO adding more than $68 billion in deficits within weeks of taking office, and criticised the abolition of ARENA after more than $400 million was already stripped from it, alongside a $50 million cut to the Partners in Recovery mental health program.

speeches.speaker: Fiona Scott
speeches.brief: Detailed a $3.5 billion, 10-year commitment to Western Sydney roads and infrastructure covering her Lindsay electorate, including WestConnex funding, announced $12 million for a new Western Sydney Community and Sports Centre, and $300,000 for CCTV cameras across Penrith and St Marys shopping strips.

speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: Said the budget will repay nearly $300 billion of Labor's debt over 10 years, saving about $16 billion a year in interest, highlighted a $20 billion medical research future fund, and detailed a $10,000 incentive for employers who hire long-term unemployed workers over 50.

speeches.speaker: Bruce Billson
speeches.brief: Highlighted a 1.5 per cent company tax cut benefiting 800,000 small businesses structured as companies, said the ACCC needed an emergency injection of more than $90 million after being left technically insolvent, and noted only 9.4 per cent of Frankston residents hold a bachelor degree or higher, proposing a new polytechnic combining Monash University and Chisholm TAFE to lift that.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Closed the appropriation bills debate detailing just under $88.4 billion in total spending including $28.3 billion for Defence and $4.3 billion for Immigration and Border Protection, noted it had been 167 days without an illegal boat arrival and nine detention centres closed, and confirmed $500,000 for CCTV cameras in Wagga Wagga under the Safer Streets Program.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Moved to amend the debate management motion for the appropriation bills to allow a later amendment to Appropriation Bill No. 6 correcting a schedule omitted due to a printing error by the Office of Parliamentary Counsel, and thanked the opposition for not opposing the motion.
